title: Siouxsie and the Banshees
wiki_lead:
Siouxsie and the Banshees ( SU-zi-and-the-BAN-shees) were a British rock band formed in London in 1976 by vocalist Siouxsie Sioux and bassist Steven Severin. The Times called them "one of the most audacious and uncompromising musical adventurers of the post-punk era".
With guitarist John McKay and drummer Kenny Morris, they created "a form of post-punk discord full of daring rhythmic and sonic experimentation". Their debut album The Scream (1978) received widespread acclaim. Following membership changes, including the addition of guitarist John McGeoch and drummer Budgie, they changed their musical direction and became one of the most successful alternative pop groups of the 1980s. Their third album Kaleidoscope (1980) peaked at number 5 on the UK Albums Chart. With Juju (1981) which also reached the top 10, they became an influence on the emerging gothic scene.
The band made a breakthrough in North America with the multifaceted album Peepshow (1988), which received critical praise. With substantial support from alternative rock radio stations, they achieved a mainstream hit in the US in 1991 with the pop single "Kiss Them for Me". Siouxsie and the Banshees' other best-known songs include "Hong Kong Garden" (1978), "Happy House" (1980), "Spellbound" (1981), "Cities in Dust" (1985) and "Peek-a-Boo" (1988). During their career, Siouxsie and the Banshees released 11 studio albums and 30 singles. The band experienced several line-up changes, with Siouxsie and Severin being the only constant members. They disbanded in 1996.
The band were post-punk pioneers. They have been widely influential, both on contemporaries and later acts. They have been cited as an influence by  bands such as Joy Division, the Cure, U2, Radiohead, and singers such as Tricky and Jeff Buckley.

History


Formation (1976–1977)
Siouxsie Sioux and Steven Severin met at a Roxy Music concert in September 1975, at a time when glam rock had faded and there was nothing new coming through with which they could identify. From February 1976, Siouxsie, Severin and some friends began to follow an unsigned band, the Sex Pistols. Journalist Caroline Coon dubbed them the "Bromley Contingent", as most of them came from the Bromley area of south-east London, a label Severin came to despise. "There was no such thing, it was just a bunch of people drawn together by the way they felt and they looked". They were all inspired by the Sex Pistols and their uncompromising attitude. grok_lead: Siouxsie and the Banshees were an English post-punk band formed in London in 1976 by vocalist Siouxsie Sioux (born Susan Janet Ballion) and bassist Steven Severin, emerging as key figures in the punk scene through their affiliation with the Bromley Contingent. The duo, inspired by the Sex Pistols, debuted at the 100 Club Punk Festival in September 1976, delivering an improvised 20-minute performance that marked their chaotic entry into music. Over their two-decade career, they evolved from raw punk roots into pioneers of goth and post-punk, blending dark atmospheres, tribal rhythms, and Siouxsie Sioux's commanding, operatic vocals to create a sound that influenced countless artists and subcultures. The band's early lineup solidified with drummer Kenny Morris and guitarist John McKay, leading to their signing with Polydor Records after the release of their debut single "Hong Kong Garden" in 1978, which peaked at No. 7 on the UK Singles Chart. Their debut album, The Scream (1978), captured their abrasive post-punk energy and reached No. 12 on the UK Albums Chart, establishing them as a force beyond punk's initial wave. Subsequent releases like Join Hands (1979), Kaleidoscope (1980, No. 5 UK), and Juju (1981) refined their style with intricate guitar work and exotic influences, while lineup changesâincluding the addition of guitarist John McGeoch in 1980 and drummer Budgie in 1979âbrought greater musical sophistication. A notable collaboration occurred in 1983 when Robert Smith of The Cure temporarily joined as guitarist for the album Hyaena (1984), further bridging post-punk and emerging goth aesthetics. By the mid-1980s, Siouxsie and the Banshees had achieved commercial success and critical acclaim with albums such as Tinderbox (1986), featuring the hit single " Cities in Dust," and Peepshow (1988), produced by Stephen Hague, which incorporated pop elements while retaining their gothic edge. Later works like Superstition (1991) and The Rapture (1995) experimented with psychedelia and electronica, showcasing their adaptability amid the Britpop era. Throughout their tenure, Siouxsie Sioux's iconic imageâmarked by bold makeup, elaborate costumes, and a fierce stage presenceâhelped define goth fashion and female empowerment in rock, drawing from influences like glam rock, David Bowie, and world music. The band disbanded in 1996 after releasing eleven studio albums, three live albums, and numerous singles, citing a desire to end on a high note with dignity following internal tensions and creative exhaustion. They briefly reunited for the Seven Year Itch compilation tour in 2002, performing hits like "Spellbound" and "Peek-a-Boo." Their legacy endures as foundational to goth rock, with Siouxsie Sioux continuing her solo career and Severin pursuing production and side projects; in October 2025, a limited-edition CD reissue of the 2022 compilation All Souls, curated by Siouxsie, was released, while the band's innovative sound and visual style remain touchstones for alternative music.
